guidelines.detail: kept for this example only, tied to it by: station
general guideline covering EXS-026 (example 18) and this example

same as LRN-043 (The description says the waiter readies a cart while the kitchen and sommelier work, and delivery waits for the food, wine and cart. The reference models the cart preparation as its own task joined by a parallel gateway (M1, F1), and the generated model has no such task. This is a real structural difference. The other records do not support a guideline: X1 (guest call as a start event) is a valid )

refines FID-02 (M2 shows the reference keeps the deferred billing as its own task, while the generated model routes the waiter's conditional choice only to the other pending work (X3) and drops the postponed activity. S11 states the deferral explicitly, so the stated activity should stay visible as a task. FID-02 already requires preserving described actions and dependencies. This guideline adds the specific case)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one branch or outcome of a decision is followed by several separately named actions performed by different actors or departments (for example, one actor receives materials while another department sets something up), joined by 'and' or 'and also': Model each separately named action as its own task in that branch, with one task per actor action, and do not merge them into one task, even when the actions are described in the same sentence. Place the tasks in parallel after the branch's split, and join them with a parallel gateway when the description requires all of them to be completed before the process continues.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an actor is assigned a work item, and a later sentence says that the same actor also has a further responsibility or activity that runs while other parties work on the same item, with the next step requiring all of that work to be done

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an actor returns to a station or location after an action, and that a later named action by that actor may be postponed while the actor handles another pending item, so the later action follows only when no other item is pending: Model the actor's return as its own task in the actor's lane, placed after the action that precedes it. Model the postponement as a decision after the return that checks whether another item is pending. Route the pending-item case to its own task in the actor's lane, and route the no-pending case to the postponed named action as its own task. Connect the flow back so that the postponed action is kept as a described task, and do not drop it because it depends on a condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an actor returns to a station or location after an action, and that a later named action by that actor may be postponed while the actor handles another pending item, so the later action follows only when no other item is pending

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that, while several parallel activities run for the same case, one actor also performs a separate action that is not part of those activities, and the later step must wait for this action as well.: Model that separate action as its own task on a dedicated parallel branch that starts at the same parallel gateway as the other parallel activities. Rejoin all branches at one parallel gateway before the later step that depends on them. Do not fold the action into another task or into the task that precedes the split, and do not omit it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that, while several parallel activities run for the same case, one actor also performs a separate action that is not part of those activities, and the later step must wait for this action as well.
rules_sent_back.source: learned guideline (refines FID-02), generalized from EXS-026

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an actor may postpone a stated activity while other pending work is handled, so the activity happens only on a condition: Model the postponable activity itself as a task labeled with the activity named in the description. Place it on the branch that the stated condition selects, behind an exclusive decision gateway whose outcomes separate the postponed case from the immediate case. Do not reduce the deferral to a gateway branch that leads only to the other pending work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an actor may postpone a stated activity while other pending work is handled, so the activity happens only on a condition
